In mathematics, a '''superpartient ratio''', also called  '''superpartient number''' or '''epimeric ratio''', is a [[rational number]] that is greater than one and is not [[superparticular number|superparticular]]. The term has fallen out of use in modern pure mathematics, but continues to be used in [[music theory]] and in the [[history of mathematics|historical study of mathematics]].

Superpartient ratios were written about by [[Nicomachus]] in his treatise ''[[Introduction to Arithmetic]]''. 

==Overview==
Mathematically, a '''superpartient number''' is a [[ratio]] of the form
:<math> \frac{n + a}{n}\, , </math>
where ''a'' is greater than 1 (''a'' > 1) and is also [[coprime]] to ''n''. Ratios of the form <math>\tfrac{n+1}{n}</math> are also greater than one and fully reduced, but are called [[superparticular number|superparticular ratios]] and are not superpartient.

|}

==Etymology==
''Superpartient'' is a [[calque]] from [[Ancient Greek|Greek]] ἐπιμερής ''epimeres'' "containing a whole and a fraction".
